hypothesis: A five-asset shared-account canary restricted to six explicitly selected bidirectional routes may produce cleaner and more frequent forward evidence than v28's mixture of 23 executable mappings, while preserving one-position-per-asset isolation and exact backend telemetry.
decision: Retain v29 as inactive and unchanged after the fixed common-window diagnostic. The exact 22.36-day overlap remains positive under nominal and stressed modeled friction, with 97 and 98 accepted lifecycles respectively, but it does not establish broad six-route edge. SPCX Swing/HA supplies 65.48% of positive nominal route PnL and 62.34% under stress, specifically through its long side while its short side loses. ETH precompression pullback and SP500 breakout pressure are negative in both scenarios, and SOL Range Onset has only two long entries and no short entry. The common window removes the prior unequal-window SOL concentration as the dominant explanation but replaces it with a different concentrated, directional dependency. This warrants mechanism-specific forward validation rather than automatic promotion, pruning, restart, drain, order, close, resize, or protection changes.
falsifier: The diagnostic is invalidated by any mismatch in the frozen v29 profile fingerprint, six-route scope, source hashes, common half-open entry interval, opened development/validation phase contract, shared-equity reconciliation, one-position-per-asset ownership, five-slot ceiling, route-side attribution, friction-path population accounting, or report-only authority. Its economic interpretation is updated by a fresh private-fill event replay or forward live sample that removes or worsens the measured SPCX-long concentration, supplies missing SOL-short evidence, reverses the negative ETH-pullback or SP500 components, produces nonpositive aggregate after-cost PnL or profit factor at or below one, materially increases drawdown or friction, or demonstrates unmodeled opposite-intent exits. These remain reported trial results rather than implicit runtime gates.
limitations: The fixed common window uses already-opened development and validation evidence and is not a sealed holdout or a future-profit forecast.
The 22.36-day interval was selected after inspecting route entry coverage, so it removes unequal calendar exposure but does not provide independent out-of-sample evidence.
Nominal and stress HIP-3 lifecycle populations differ by one SPCX short because friction-dependent exit timing changes later entry eligibility; the stress result is not a pure fee-only sensitivity.
Precomputed independent exits cannot reproduce an opposite provider closing an owned same-asset lifecycle early.
HIP-3 entry cash reservation approximates the entry leg as half of observed round-trip fees while each source net PnL remains after-cost.
Completed-bar replay cannot establish private IOC fills, queue position, acknowledgement latency, stop gaps, or future funding and slippage.
Realized-equity drawdown omits concurrent intratrade mark-to-market paths and liquidation-path stress.
The positive aggregate is materially concentrated in SPCX Swing/HA long outcomes and does not prove edge for the SPCX short side, ETH pullback, or SP500 breakout pressure.
SOL Range Onset has only two long lifecycles and no short lifecycle in the common interval, so its bidirectional behavior is unresolved.
No live route, process, order, position, stop, target, allocation, transition drain, or protection changed in this revision.
